extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, advocates, agency staff, and policymakers (attorneys and stakeholders working on public-charge/admissibility determinations)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the regulatory/evidentiary criteria and sources DHS uses to evaluate public‑charge inadmissibility determinations (statutory minimum factors, evidentiary forms, sponsor/household income rules, and related CFR/INA citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Health factor — use of Form I-693
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will collect information relevant to the statutory minimum factors from existing information collections, e.g., information pertaining to the health factor will be obtained from Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM indicated that the medical examination report (Form I-693) would be considered as source information for the health factor; related authorities cited include 42 CFR 34.3 and 34.4. (Page cites multiple places noting the I-693 as a source DHS will use.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Household income excludes public benefits and unlawful-source income
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's household income, assets, and liabilities excludes income from public benefits listed in 8 CFR 212.21(b) as well as income or assets from illegal activities or sources such as proceeds from illegal gambling or drug sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion is reflected in the regulations and cross-referenced guidance (e.g., 8 CFR 212.21(b); 8 CFR 212.22(a)(1)(iv)). The citations also point to Form/affidavit rules that bar counting unlawful-source income (see I-864 instructions and 8 CFR references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support (Section 213A) may be considered but is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute permits, but does not require, the consideration of a sufficient Affidavit of Support under section 213A of the INA, if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: INA sec. 212(a)(4)(B)(i) and (ii) and related discussions (multiple places note that an affidavit may be considered but is not mandatory). The page references Form I-134 and I-864 contexts where affidavits/support are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor must demonstrate means to maintain income (tax returns or assets)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sponsor demonstrates the means to maintain income by presenting Federal income tax returns or by demonstrating significant assets of the sponsored immigrant or of the sponsor, if such assets are available for the support of the sponsored immigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority and cross-references include INA sec. 213A(f)(6), 8 CFR 213a.2(c)(2)(ii), and DHS discussion at 87 FR citations; DHS notes tax returns or documented assets as typical evidence of means to support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-864/I-134 instructions prohibit relying on income from illegal acts
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS instructions for the Affidavit of Support (I-864) prohibit the sponsor from relying on a household member's income from illegal acts (such as proceeds from illegal gambling or drug sales) to meet the income requirement even if the household member paid taxes on that income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited source: USCIS 'Instructions for Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA' (OMB Control No. 1615-0075) and related 8 CFR provisions (e.g., 8 CFR 213a.1 and 8 CFR 204.6 cross-references).

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS will use existing information collections to obtain evidence for statutory minimum factors
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will collect information relevant to the statutory minimum factors from existing information collections (the NPRM expressly noted that existing forms/reports will be used to supply data for the statutory factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: information pertaining to the health factor will be obtained from Form I-693. Multiple citations to 87 FR (Feb. 24, 2022) explain DHS's plan to rely on existing collections rather than create wholly new collections for those factors.
